name: add_php_validator_stop_on_first_field_failure
description: Validator chain gains per-field stop-on-first-failure so a later rule on an already-failed field doesn't also fire; broken stops ALL validation instead of just that one field
prompts: Validator::validate() in validator.php runs every registered rule unconditionally, even when an earlier rule on the SAME field already failed - so a chain like ->rule('email', 'required')->rule('email', 'looks like an email') runs the format check on a null value too, adding a confusing second error for a field that's simply missing. Change validate() to skip any FURTHER rules for a field once one of its rules has failed, while rules for OTHER fields are completely unaffected and all still run. Keep the public interface (rule()/validate()) and the error-message ordering (registration order) unchanged.

setup_files.validator.php:
<?php

class Validator
{
    private array $rules = [];

    public function rule(string $field, callable $check, string $message): self
    {
        $this->rules[] = [$field, $check, $message];
        return $this;
    }

    /** @return string[] error messages, in rule-registration order */
    public function validate(array $data): array
    {
        $errors = [];
        foreach ($this->rules as [$field, $check, $message]) {
            $value = $data[$field] ?? null;
            if (!$check($value)) {
                $errors[] = $message;
            }
        }
        return $errors;
    }
}

test_setup_files.hidden_test.php:
<?php
require __DIR__ . '/validator.php';

function assertEqualArrays(array $expected, array $actual, string $msg): void
{
    if ($expected !== $actual) {
        fwrite(STDERR, "$msg\nexpected: " . json_encode($expected) . "\nactual:   " . json_encode($actual) . "\n");
        exit(1);
    }
}

$v = (new Validator())
    ->rule('email', fn($v) => $v !== null, 'email is required')
    ->rule('email', fn($v) => $v === null || str_contains($v, '@'), 'email must contain @')
    ->rule('age', fn($v) => $v !== null, 'age is required');

// email missing entirely: the FORMAT check must not also fire (it would
// crash-equivalent / confuse on a null value) - only ONE email error, plus
// the unrelated age error (a different field, unaffected by email's failure)
assertEqualArrays(
    ['email is required', 'age is required'],
    $v->validate(['age' => null]),
    'missing email should short-circuit to one email error, plus the age error',
);

// email present but malformed: only the format rule fails (the required
// rule for email already passed)
assertEqualArrays(
    ['email must contain @'],
    $v->validate(['email' => 'not-an-email', 'age' => 30]),
    'malformed email only',
);

// everything valid
assertEqualArrays([], $v->validate(['email' => 'a@b.com', 'age' => 30]), 'all valid');

echo "PASS\n";

reference_solution.validator.php:
<?php

class Validator
{
    private array $rules = [];

    public function rule(string $field, callable $check, string $message): self
    {
        $this->rules[] = [$field, $check, $message];
        return $this;
    }

    /**
     * Runs rules in registration order but STOPS at the first field that
     * fails - a chain like ->rule('email', 'required')->rule('email', 'looks
     * like an email') must not run the format check (and crash or produce a
     * confusing second error) on a field that is already known to be
     * missing. Rules on DIFFERENT fields are unaffected by one field's
     * failure and all still run.
     *
     * @return string[] error messages, in rule-registration order
     */
    public function validate(array $data): array
    {
        $errors = [];
        $failedFields = [];
        foreach ($this->rules as [$field, $check, $message]) {
            if (in_array($field, $failedFields, true)) {
                continue;
            }
            $value = $data[$field] ?? null;
            if (!$check($value)) {
                $errors[] = $message;
                $failedFields[] = $field;
            }
        }
        return $errors;
    }
}

files.validator.php:
<?php

class Validator
{
    private array $rules = [];

    public function rule(string $field, callable $check, string $message): self
    {
        $this->rules[] = [$field, $check, $message];
        return $this;
    }

    public function validate(array $data): array
    {
        $errors = [];
        foreach ($this->rules as [$field, $check, $message]) {
            $value = $data[$field] ?? null;
            if (!$check($value)) {
                $errors[] = $message;
                break;
            }
        }
        return $errors;
    }
}
